content:
Hi Rebecca,

It's not a change and it's not a matter of policy. It's how the technology works. Thunderbird is an "e-mail client". E-mail clients work by accessing users' accounts at servers run by e-mail service providers. They retrieve mail from those accounts and send mail from those accounts. So, as Lin says, access to the accounts is required. Without it, Thunderbird cannot fetch or send messages for you (or use your address books or manage your calendar).

content:
Just so we're starting off on the right foot...

- You're in the "~/.var/app/org.mozilla.thunderbird/.thunderbird/" (also known as "/home/lsprague/.var/app/org.mozilla.thunderbird/.thunderbird" folder. You will see a few other folders, including your "former Windows profile" (profile names are arbitrary - they can be named anything), and most importantly, there will be a file named "profiles.ini".

- Start Thunderbird. If it's the first time you have started it you may be prompted to set up an account. You don't need to do this, so decline the invitation.

- If the menu bar is hidden, press Alt to reveal it, and choose <Help | Troubleshooting Information>. Scroll down to where you find Profiles - and click on "about:profiles" to bring up the About Profiles screen.

- Press the "Create New Profile" - this starts the Create Profile Wizard. Click Next to begin...

- It's important that you do this part in order:

a) Enter you new profile name - this can be anything you want, like your real name or whatever.

b) click "Choose folder..." Inconveniently, you will have to navigate back to the "~/.var/app/org.mozilla.thunderbird/.thunderbird" folder. If you have the Files browser set to show hidden files, you will see the .var folder and can navigate from there. When you reach your destination, select your FORMER_WINDOWS_PROFILE and click the Select button.

c) this takes you back the the previous dialog box. Confirm that "Your user settings (...) will be stored in:" is the "former Windows profile you just selected. If that looks good, click Finish

- You will now be back at the About Profiles screen. When you scroll down you will see your newly-added profile, and it will say, "Default Profile: yes".

- Now scroll back up and click the "Restart Normally" button. Thunderbird will restart using your new/old Windows profile, and you should be back in business. (LATER EDIT! DON'T USE THE "RESTART NORMALLY BUTTON. JUST QUIT THUNDER BIRD AND RESTART IT)

I will attach an animation of the process if it's not too big...
